keep_playing_why: In B the goal was clear in 15 seconds and every drift or smash threw up a score pop-up, so I felt rewarded early and often. In A I died with zero kills in the first minute to attackers I could not see, lost score each death, and only got going after about 4 minutes of working out Bloom. B's world changes from sunset to rain to a tunnel kept me wanting the next mile.
better_made_why: B looks and sounds like a finished arcade racer, with clear instructions on screen, strong time-of-day and weather changes, and rich feedback on each smash and drift. A has gorgeous painted art and the colour-bloom is a lovely idea, but shots give almost no visible hit feedback, damage comes from unseen sources, and the first message points to a gold mark that is hard to find.
furthest_A: Still on the first objective (Break the inkwell in the Olive Terraces, 'Nodes open' reached once after clearing a wave), score 45,231, 1.4% restored, died many times.
furthest_B: Mile 45, in-game clock 01:42 (dawn at 06:00 not reached), score 7,750, through golden hour, blue hour, night, rain, a tunnel and a convenience store, many crashes and magnet rescues on the way.
